summary: Revise, not reject. The exact SHA-identified asymmetric decoder and its popularity-tail corollary are mathematically sound over F_p^2 for every integer 100<d<p, including the conversion to one global polynomial. The exponent ledger is correct: the unconditional exponent remains 1/3, while the additional popularity hypothesis gives conditional exponent 1/(a+2), up to 1/2. Strict acceptance fails because P11 omits the admissible star-order range and contains a false unqualified Theta(epsilon^2) side claim; the KTZ general-field notation also needs correction. These issues are repairable and do not constitute a fatal obstruction to the hashed theorem.
